request.text: My rosemary smells much stronger just after I brush against it. Is the plant releasing more scent because I touched it, or am I simply noticing what was already there?

responsibilities.outcome: Explain in accessible terms why touching rosemary can make its aroma seem stronger, while distinguishing physical release of aromatic compounds from increased human attention to the scent.

semantic_facts: The explanation should convey that brushing rosemary can disturb or rupture surface oil glands and release additional volatile aromatic compounds.
It may also note that the user's proximity and attention can amplify perception, so both release and noticing can contribute.
forbidden_claims: The assistant presents scent release as evidence that the plant is frightened, conscious, or sending a deliberate message.
The assistant claims to have touched or inspected the user's rosemary.

target.claim_boundary: assistant-authored candidate oracle; not independently reviewed

negative_hypotheses: A straightforward causal explanation is unnecessarily converted into an observation or action workflow.
The response gives an anthropomorphic certainty instead of separating plant chemistry from human perception.
